utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we are encroaching on the time of --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: One more question. We are likely to be expelled if we don't leave.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question. Just one more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said, I noted it down when you spoke about those various documents, you said you did not torpedo documents because there was a core to them with which you agreed. So you didn't torpedo documents because there was a core to them with which you could agree. That's what you said when you spoke of the Contact Group. Tell me, what is the core with which you agreed?

utterances.speaker: YEVGENY PRIMAKOV
utterances.text: I would like to clarify one point. This doesn't apply to all the documents of the Contact Group. Some documents were passed unconditionally by all, but there were also some documents that didn't suit us completely on all points, but we thought it was a lesser evil and it would be more useful to accept them despite the fact that certain parts of those documents did not exactly suit us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Primakov --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since Mr. Nice, speaking of Rambouillet, trivialised everything to the point that he made everything seem to hinge on one word, military or not military. Tell me one thing: When the Russian representative in Rambouillet put his signature to the draft, is it true that he said "except annexes 2 and 7"? Is it true, in other words, that even the Russian representative declined to sign annexes 2 and 7, envisaging the presence of NATO troops in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Of course it's a leading question. It also completely mischaracterises the exchange between the witness and myself, the witness having himself settled upon the word "military" as the sole defining reason for the change of heart of the accused. But given the pressure of time, if the Court wants the witness to answer the question as formulated, I'm not going to take any further time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: A very brief answer and that will be the final -- this is the final question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already lost the thread. What was -- what were we talking about? I was listening to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Primakov, is it the case that in Rambouillet, not even the Russian representative was willing to sign annexes 2 and 7 relating to military presence?

utterances.speaker: YEVGENY PRIMAKOV
utterances.text: My answer will be yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Primakov, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mechanics of the exhibit: It's been put together in the form in order to be a helpful document that contains everything on a particular topic in one place. Now, that may or may not be what you would prefer. It may or not be helpful but that's the basis upon which it was done. We've identified in it all the existing -- in the index, we've identified all the documents that have already been produced, so that one course would be to allow this to be an exhibit as it stands and then it's just a file of basically NATO security -- Contact Group, Security Council documents and one or two others where we can find everything. Alternatively, we'll filet out everything that's been produced already.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be 795, and I'm going to pull out those exhibits which are already into the evidence. So it's going to be 11 tabs, tab 1 to tab 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or we can use the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The existing tab numbers might be easier for the purposes of the record, and then if the Registry would allow the existing index to travel with the exhibit, people will always understand what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's preferable.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'd like to inform the parties that there is a plenary next week Wednesday, so we'll sit on Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Please take note, Mr. Milosevic. We are adjourned.
